name: room
text: Room opened — goal: mining: Gather AI info from DIVERSE sources (GitHub/HN/Product Hunt/Reddit/Telegram/social), NOT j

name: Pick
text:
I’ll mine GitHub for AI projects with >100 stars created in the last 30 days. Command:
`gh search repos --q "ai language:python stars:>100 pushed:>2024-05-01" --json name,url,stargazers_count --limit 50 > github_ai_top50.json`

Then I’ll scrape Hacker News top 100 AI stories from the last week via Algolia API (`https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?query=ai&tags=story&numericFilters=created_at_i>1716768000`) and save to `hn_ai_top100.json`.

name: Assay
text: Assay: Your GitHub query risks **false precision**—`pushed:>2024-05-01` filters *commits*, not *project inception*, so a 2023 repo with a single May commit could pollute results. Where’s the evidence that 100+ stars + recent activity correlates with *current* AI relevance? And why scrape HN *after* GitHub? The room’s "DIVERSE sources" mandate demands parallel mining—your sequential approach risks bias toward code-heavy projects while missing discourse-driven trends. Show me the failure modes.
